$comment: The capabilities a C ABI host supplies through its host-service channel, and the numbers each
travels under (include/migo/host_services.h).
WHY THIS EXISTS. Ads, payment, login, sharing and mini-program navigation are not the engine's to
implement: each is the host app's own integration with a vendor SDK, a store or a backend. On
Android the Java SDK carries them as typed handler interfaces. Every other platform Migo ships --
Apple, Linux, Windows, OpenHarmony -- embeds the C ABI, which had no way to carry them at all, so
content there got `not supported` for every one. The channel is one callback, one completion and
one event entry point; this file is what gives its three integers meaning.
WHY JSON PAYLOADS. These option sets are open and vendor-shaped -- an ad unit's options, a
payment's offer and zone, a share's title and image -- and they are already JSON on every other
path: the engine's service traits take it, and the Java SDK receives it. Small closed option sets
(the keyboard, vibration) stay typed structs, where a host should not need a JSON parser.
RULES. Append only. A service, method or event number is never reused and never renumbered: a
host built against one header and a library built against another must still mean the same call
by the same numbers. A service's number is also its bit in MigoHostCallbacks.host_services, so
service ids stay below 64.
A `command` is fire-and-forget: the host carries it out and replies to nothing. A `call` carries
a nonzero call_id the host must complete exactly once with
migo_session_complete_host_service_call. A failure carries the host's reason, which content
composes into its errMsg (`<api>:fail <reason>`) itself: one method can serve several content APIs
-- a subpackage download is both loadSubpackage and preDownloadSubpackage -- so no name here could
be right for all of them. `error_code_field` names the field a failure's numeric code is delivered
in, or null where the content API defines none. `hook` is where the engine delivers the result or
the event to content; the host never names one. `op` is the engine op that makes the request,
which the gate checks still exists.
A call may report progress while in flight (migo_session_update_host_service_call), delivered
to `progress_hook`. `withheld` names result fields the engine keeps rather than delivers: a
downloaded subpackage's `zipPath` is a host path that must never reach content, so the engine
records it for the install and strips it.
Checked by engine/crates/capi/src/host_services.rs's tests (the Rust table) and
scripts/test-host-services-contract.sh (the C header, the ops and the hooks).
